iso8601.description: Similar to the standard date type, but each section after the year is optional. e.g. 2014-06-29 or 2023-04

description.description: Write a short description about the job

address.description: To add multiple address lines, use \n. For example, 1234 Glücklichkeit Straße\nHinterhaus 5. Etage li.

countryCode.description: code as per ISO-3166-1 ALPHA-2, e.g. US, AU, IN

region.description: The general region where you live. Can be a US state, or a province, for instance.

remote.description: the level of remote work available

salary.description: The pay as the post words it, for display, e.g. '$120k–150k + equity'. Structured amounts go in compensation (#319)

compensation.description: The pay as numbers, for tools (#319). salary stays the text people read. Values normalised to one currency are derived data, not part of the document

min.description: The lowest amount offered, per period

max.description: The highest amount offered, per period; equal to min for a single figure

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD, EUR, AUD

period.description: What each amount is paid for

facets.description: The post in fixed terms tools can filter on (#353). Each is optional, and unspecified means the post does not say. The free-text fields above stay for display

remoteScope.description: Where the work is done: remote_region is remote within named regions, remote_global remote from anywhere

remoteRegions.description: Where remote work is allowed, when limited, e.g. ['US'], ['EU']

timezoneRange.description: Hours of overlap or time zones required, e.g. UTC-5 to UTC+1

visaSponsorship.description: Whether the employer sponsors a visa

salaryProvenance.description: Whether compensation comes from numbers the post states, was inferred, or is missing

items.description: e.g. Build out a new API for our customer base.

keywords.description: List some keywords pertaining to this skill

meta.description: The schema version and any other tooling configuration lives here

canonical.description: URL (as per RFC 3986) to latest version of this document

version.description: A version field which follows semver - e.g. v1.0.0
